jobs.title: Program Coordinator, Equitable Building Decarbonization Program
jobs.description:
Job Title: Program Coordinator – Equitable Building Decarbonization Program  
Primary Work Location: San Francisco – Bay Area (Hybrid)  
FLSA Classification: Exempt  
Projected Salary Range: $55,000 - $75,000

Overview: Association for Energy Affordability (AEA) is a rapidly growing national nonprofit energy services and training organization dedicated to reducing the carbon impact of the built environment while fostering and maintaining affordable and healthy housing and communities. Energy consulting services are completed through AEA’s participation in a variety of federal, state, and local energy programs and initiatives. For more information about AEA, see http://www.aea.us.org.

Position Summary: AEA West is seeking a Program Coordinator to join our tight-knit, talented team of “Energy Geeks”. The candidate must be passionate about energy efficiency and green building, highly organized, detail-oriented, and have strong communication skills.
  
  
The Program Coordinator will assist one or more of AEA’s Program Associates and/or Program Managers in the day-to-day operations and process flow of programs directed at providing energy efficiency and building decarbonization services for multifamily buildings. The Program Coordinator will work collaboratively with AEA’s Program Associates and/ or Program Managers who manage and support program implementation oversee and coordinate with technical staff, analyze program and pilot data, coordinate with external parties, conduct outreach and intake. The Program Coordinator engages in project scheduling, marketing and outreach, data analysis, report production, special program projects/ pilots, and database management as needed to deliver high impact energy efficiency and building decarbonization programs. They are expected to be a self-starter, an independent problem solver, and a strong team-player with a customer-service orientation.

AEA is hiring for primary work locations based in the Bay Area. Candidates must have the ability to travel within California upon request.

Responsibilities:
  
The Program Coordinator may be expected to assist with:

* Supporting energy efficiency, renewable energy and/or building decarbonization program implementation.
* Supporting technical staff conducting energy audits and in-field energy assessments, on-site diagnostics, field data collection and analysis as needed.
* Gathering, analyzing, and reporting program data such as program pipeline, measure savings, benchmarking and other utility data, project savings, regional project distribution, etc.
* Implementing special projects within a program.
* Conducting outreach and intake to program participants and stakeholders.
* Developing program materials, forms, process documents.
* Supporting invoicing and budget reconciliation
* Supporting data entry and data quality control
* Developing and updating marketing materials, email templates, presentations and websites.
* Communicating about the program to stakeholders including inquiries received from general program email inbox and hotline as well as representing the program at conferences and in-person events and tours as needed.

These job responsibilities may be revised over time to ensure the functional responsiveness of the Program Coordinator to AEA and Federal and California State program requirements.

Minimum Qualifications:  

* Bachelor’s degree or an Associate degree.
* One (1) year of related experience in a related role.
* Basic knowledge and experience in energy efficiency and green building principles.
* Strong oral and written communication skills.
* Ability to bring together various resources to work together collaboratively.
* Advanced-level knowledge of MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

Additional Qualifications Desired:  

* Basic knowledge and understanding of Title 24 and other building codes and standards.
* Familiarity with local, state, and federal incentive and rebate programs.
* Sound technical writing skills and experience.
* Proficiency in Salesforce.

Must be able to legally work in the country where this position is located without visa sponsorship.

**EEO Non-Discrimination and ADA Reasonable Accommodation Statement:**  
Applicants are considered for all positions without regard to race, color, creed, religion, age, national origin, immigration or citizenship status, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital or partnership status, disability, military status, veteran status, or predisposing genetic characteristics. AEA does not discriminate on the basis of physical or mental disability where the essential functions of the job can be reasonably accommodated. Determinations on requests for reasonable accommodation will be made on a case-by-case basis. For more information on the physical requirements of this position and/or if you need reasonable accommodation for any part of the application and hiring process, please notify Human Resources at 718-292-6733 ext. 8265.

We maintain an inclusive culture where everyone feels safe to contribute and help us innovate, and we encourage people from diverse backgrounds to apply to our roles.

TO APPLY: Interested applicants must submit a cover letter and resume to be considered. In your cover letter, please share examples of AEA’s past or current work that is most exciting to you and why. We will not be reviewing resumes without a cover letter.

You may find all our open positions at our Careers site here: https://aea.us.org/about/#careers

AEA offers excellent benefits, including medical/dental/vision, commuter plan, 401(k) w/matching contribution, generous PTO, educational assistance, paid parental leave, hybrid work arrangement and many development opportunities. We are also an eligible employer for student loan forgiveness.

jobs.title: PROGRAM COORDINATOR
jobs.description:
**The Opportunity**

Come join our team! Homeward Bound helps unsheltered individuals and families in Marin County transform their lives through housing, training, and supportive services.

Homeward Bound is Marin County’s primary provider of shelter and housing for individuals and families experiencing homelessness. We offer emergency shelter, short- and long-term supportive housing, job training and placement, and wraparound services. Our mission is **Opening Doors to Safety, Dignity, Hope, and Independence**.

We are seeking a **Program Coordinator** to join our Nuestra Casa Family Program.

**Principal Responsibilities**

* Provide housing-focused case management for participants of Nuestra Casa Family Program.
* Facilitate client groups and events across the team’s housing portfolio.
* Incorporate **intensive care coordination and housing stabilization strategies** into individualized housing and care plans, in collaboration with healthcare, behavioral health, and community-based partners.
* Identify and address barriers to housing stabilization, including chronic homelessness, mental and physical health needs, substance use disorders, under-employment, lack of income, and other systemic barriers.
* Skillfully prevent and/or resolve conflicts skillfully using a strengths-based approach.
* Respond to urgent and crisis situations, including coordination with EMTs, fire, law enforcement, psychiatric services, and community partners as needed.
* Prevent and resolve conflicts using a strengths-based, trauma-informed approach.
* Provide supportive services, guidance, and referrals to community resources.
* Engage program participants regularly and consistently to support program participation and progress toward housing stability.

**Documentation and Compliance**

* Complete timely, accurate, and compliant documentation, including billable case notes, assessments, care plans, and progress updates, in accordance with policies and funder requirements.
* Ensure client records clearly demonstrate eligibility, service delivery, engagement, and progress toward housing, health, and personal goals.
* Maintain accurate and timely data entry in HIPPO (Salesforce database) and HMIS.
* Meet all documentation and case management deadlines, including intake, enrollment, reassessments, housing goals, and discharge documentation.
* Participate in quality assurance, monitoring, and audit processes, including responding to documentation reviews and corrective actions.

**Case Management, Housing-Focused Services, and Outcomes**

* Develop, implement, and regularly update individualized, client-centered housing and care plans.
* Monitor, document, and adjust plans proactively to address changing needs or barriers.
* Coordinate services with internal teams and external partners to ensure continuity of care and timely referrals.
* Document housing and service outcomes to support program performance measurement and funder reporting.
* Develop, implement, and monitor financial literacy services tailored to covering topics such as budgeting, credit repair, savings strategies, and employment preparedness.
* Assist program participants in housing retention, job readiness skills, job placement and retention services, education on living skills, navigating resources and referrals, eviction diversion, and addressing physical and mental health issues.

**Property Management and Housing Placement**

* Assist the Senior Director of Family Programs and Program Manager with client identification and screening for housing eligibility, leasing, and client move-ins
* Assist the Senior Director with refining program policies and practices, unit setup and purchasing, and facility troubleshooting
* Promptly submit documentation to the Marin Housing Authority for the issuance of client vouchers and rental calculations/recalculations as needed
* Assist with property management, including but not limited to creating and tracking maintenance requests, maintaining site presence across the housing campus, tracking client rental payments, issuing legal notices, and documenting tenancy challenges
* Proactively monitor building needs, perform rounds, coordinate closely with facilities

**Professional Standards and Team Collaboration**

* Manage a full caseload and bi-weekly/monthly meetings, with strong organization, time-management, and prioritization skills.
* Communicate clearly and professionally with supervisors, team members, volunteers, agency partners, and program participants.
* Participate in weekly supervision, program meetings, all-staff meetings, and required training.
* Maintain confidentiality and comply with all agency policies, including HIPAA where applicable.
* Contribute positively as a collaborative, accountable member of the Homeward Bound team.
* Strong organizational skills

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Education / Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in social work, psychology, social welfare, or a related field **OR** three (3) years of experience in a related residential or housing program.

**Experience & Knowledge**

* Minimum of three (3) years’ experience working with under-resourced or low-income populations; experience working with individuals experiencing homelessness preferred.
* Experience in residential and/or housing programs.
* Knowledge of Housing First and harm-reduction principles.
* Working knowledge of SSI, SSDI, and SDI.
* Working knowledge of local resources for low-income individuals.

* Comfort working in a culturally and ethnically diverse environment.
* Working knowledge of substance dependence disorders and mental health disorders.
* Ability to read and interpret documents, write routine reports and correspondence, and speak effectively before small groups of clients or employees of the organization.

jobs.title: Part Time Crossroads Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Marin Academy**

**Part-Time Crossroads Program Coordinator**

**Second semester of the 26-27 School Year**

Marin Academy seeks an experienced Educator or Program Coordinator for a part-time, after-school Program Coordinator position from
 **January 5th-May 28th, 2027.**

**Position Schedule:**

* 10 hours/week throughout the semester.
  
* Non-exempt hourly position. Compensation $28 - $33/hr.
  
* Mondays 3 - 6 p.m., Tuesdays 3–5 p.m., Thursdays 3-5 p.m.
  
* An additional 3 hours per week will be scheduled for meeting and prep time. These hours can be flexible.
  
* There will be 2-3 weekend and evening commitments throughout the semester (family workshops, field trips, celebrations, etc.).

**Overview of the Crossroads Program:**

Crossroads is an after-school program for sixth-, seventh-, and eighth-grade students attending public middle schools in San Rafael. Students apply to the program at the beginning of their 6th-grade year and commit to it for three years. The major objective of Crossroads is to equip students with the skills they need for success in middle school, high school, college, and beyond. We believe these students are at an important crossroads in their lives, and we are committed to providing them with the support, skills, and information to improve their access to educational opportunities. For more information about Crossroads, please visit
our website.

  

Crossroads is a program of Marin Academy, an independent, college preparatory high school located in San Rafael, CA, with an enrollment of approximately 450 students with academic talent, interest in the arts and athletics, and a passion for a multitude of issues. The Crossroads program was born out of Marin Academy’s mission statement, which “asks every individual to think, question, and create in an environment of encouragement and compassion, and challenges each person to accept the responsibilities posed by education in a democratic society.” The school is a vibrant and diverse community, and students and teachers alike continue to work towards furthering an inclusive and supportive school. Marin Academy students participate as tutors and teachers within the Crossroads after-school program. Marin Academy is an equal-opportunity employer, and people of color and women are encouraged to apply. For more information about Marin Academy, please visit our website (
www.ma.org
).

**Position Description & Qualifications:**

Crossroads seeks an experienced, professional candidate who is both organized in their ability to coordinate an after-school program and skilled in working with high school and middle school students. The Crossroads Program Coordinator will spend about 40% of their time organizing program logistics in the Crossroads office on the Marin Academy campus and 60% of their time providing direct service during our after-school program on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday afternoons. The Crossroads Coordinator will also do supply runs off-campus and ride the bus with students as needed. If the program is virtual at any time, the Crossroads Coordinator will support and facilitate Crossroads sessions online. Candidates must be personable, organized, independent, creative, flexible, and cooperative.

  

**Minimum Requirements**
 **:**

  

* Ability to communicate with both adults and students effectively
  
* Commitment to social justice, anti-racism, and equity in education
  
* Strong organizational skills
  
* Experience with basic computer software (Zoom, MS Office, Google Docs, Internet, Email)
  
* A valid driver’s license and willingness to drive students in school vans
  
* A valid driver’s license to do supply runs to local stores (Target, Costco, Michael’s Craft Store, Safeway, etc.)
  

  

**Desired Qualifications**
 **:**

* Spanish-speaking and writing fluency (ability to make phone calls in Spanish and translate documents)
  

  

**How to Apply:**

  

Interested applicants should submit a résumé and cover letter to the ADP site on our web page: http://www.ma.org/careers

jobs.company: Asian Americans for Civil Rights & Equality (AACRE)
jobs.title: SFILEN & SFRRN Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
### **Position Summary:**

The Program Coordinator supports the San Francisco Immigrant Legal and Education Network (SFILEN) and the San Francisco Rapid Response Network (SFRRN) by coordinating partners on grant and contract administration, meetings, and network-wide programming. The Program Coordinator occasionally fills shifts on the SFRRN Hotline, coordinates logistics and develops content and materials for reports, events, campaigns, and social media.

### 

### **About Chinese for Affirmative Action (CAA)**

CAA was founded in 1969 to protect the civil and political rights of Chinese Americans and to advance multiracial democracy in the United States. Today, CAA is a progressive voice in and on behalf of the broader Asian American and Pacific Islander community. CAA advocates for systemic change that protects immigrant rights, promotes language diversity, and remedies racial and social injustice.

### 

### **About SFILEN and SFFRN**

The San Francisco Immigrant Legal and Education Network (SFILEN) and the San Francisco Rapid Response Network (SFRRN), are two leading immigration legal service networks in the City. Since their founding in 2006 and 2008 respectively, both networks have paved the way as successful models for multi-ethnic, multi-lingual, multi-strategy coalition building to advance immigrant rights and immigrant access to legal services.

  

The San Francisco Rapid Response Network (SFRRN) is a 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, immigration enforcement response hotline serving the City of San Francisco. Founded in 2008, and revamped in 2016, SFRRN was one of the first, and remains one of the few 24/7 immigration enforcement response hotlines in the country. SFRRN houses 8 immigration focused community based organizations who staff the 24/7 hotline, verifies immigration enforcement activity in San Francisco, connects San Franciscans to legal and accompaniment services, and provides immigration centered Know-Your-Rights to immigrant community members citywide.

  

In 2026, CAA became the lead and fiscal agency to house SFILEN and SFRRN. As a founding and active member of these networks, CAA is committed to the health and wellbeing of both collaboratives in order that partners may continue to serve immigrant communities with immigration legal services and community education in the face of heightened immigration enforcement and rising xenophobia.

  

### **Position Description**

Program Coordinator coordinates partners in both SFRRN and SFILEN in relation to administration of grants and contracts and network wide programing including regularly scheduled meetings, special events, and campaigns. The Program Coordinator also coordinates logistics, and develops content and materials to support the advancement of SFILEN and SFRRN including for reports, events, campaigns, and meetings. The Coordinator works to ensure alignment and accessibility of information for all network partners and relevant stakeholders. The Program Coordinator will also assist the SFRRN Manager in supporting hotline services including receiving hotline calls, conducting follow-up, and coordinating with partners to respond to incidents of immigration enforcement.

**Key Responsibilities**

*Administrative Support for SFRRN & SFILEN Grants and Contracts*

* Communicate regularly with partners in Spanish and English about administrative requirements, reporting, and deadlines associated with funder compliance.
* Support grant and contract management through monthly data entry, compilation of partner reports, and tracking of services rendered by partners.
* Work closely with the SFILEN and SFRRN Program Managers and the AACRE Capacity Team to ensure timely reporting, invoicing, and submission of funder-required documents across all funding sources.
* Take notes at SFILEN and SFRRN meetings, conduct post-meeting follow-up, and share out notes.
* Document trends from meetings and partner reports, and identify opportunities for systems improvement.
* Transcribe all Rapid Response Hotline calls, tracking and documenting trends and identifying opportunities for systems improvement. (SFRRN)

*Programmatic Coordination of SFILEN and SFRRN*

* Support program logistics and communications for both Networks, including email reminders and coordination of monthly calls, and meetings.
* Support logistics, coordination, and planning for annual programming. This includes Immigrant Family Day, International Migrants Day, budget advocacy, retreats, trainings, and other Network-wide events and activities.

*Content and Material Development*

* Create visuals, infographics, and digital media for SFILEN and SFRRN events, campaigns, programming, and meetings. Examples include fliers, one-pagers, advocacy and fundraising materials, toolkits, and communications content.

  

*Data and Research*

* Provide timely data from SFILEN and SFRRN’s work to respective Network staff, partners, and funders, and articulate and document analyses and impact of such data.
* Assist with the collection, and coordination of data retrieved from other related immigration networks, such as the California Coalition for Immigrant Justice (CCIJ), the San Francisco Immigrant Legal Defense Collaborative (SFILDC), and other partners including intakes, statistics, reports, and referrals to inform SFILEN and SFRRN’s work.
* Conduct and/or coordinate research projects on immigration trends, immigration policy changes, relevant community resources, and other subjects.

  

*Translation*

* Translate communications and notes between English and Spanish to ensure accessibility of information across Network partners.

  

*Rapid Response Network*

* Serve as a dispatcher on the Rapid Response Hotline, where back-up is needed. This includes answering hotline phone calls, triaging emergency immigration situations, completing intake forms, and communicating with various stakeholders to coordinate service referrals.

jobs.description:
**CASE MANAGER I and II (Tagalog)**

**Case Manager I Bilingual - $2,741.57 - $3,993.25 Bi-weekly; $71,280.82 - $103,824.50 Annual**

**Case Manager II Bilingual - $2,846.40 - $4,148.14 Bi-weekly; $74,006.40 - $107,851.64 Annual**

**New hires with no prior Regional Center work experience will start at the very beginning of the salary scale.**

**\* Please note that our new hire date is anticipated to be Monday, January 4th \***

The Regional Center of the East Bay (RCEB) is one of 21 Regional Centers that are community-based, private non-profit corporations under contract with the California Department of Developmental Services. RCEB provides intake, assessment, diagnosis, and coordinates community-based services for over 25,000 children and adults with developmental disabilities in Alameda and Contra Costa counties.

RCEB envisions a future where persons with developmental disabilities are truly a part of the community. Persons with developmental disabilities receive supports and services they need to succeed. The supports and services change as the need changes.

In our dream, children with developmental disabilities live with families in typical communities. Many choose to attend their neighborhood schools and play with neighborhood friends. Adults with developmental disabilities live in the residence of their choice – with family members, with friends, or with their spouse / significant other. They engage in activities of their choice – work, volunteering, education, training, or leisure. They have meaningful relationships with friends and coworkers and are seen as valuable, contributing members of their communities.

**Key Responsibilities**:

**Case Managers** are an integral part of realizing our dream. Under general direction, Case Managers are responsible for the entire case management process, including: assessment and evaluation, planning, authorizing, advocacy, monitoring, reviewing documentation for completion.

* Facilitate the planning process and develop the Individual Program Plan (IPP) or Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) for assigned Consumers and oversee the implementation of the IPP/IFSP. Monitor and evaluate the services provided through the plan.

* Coordinate and support the implementation of the Consumers plan which may include identifying natural supports and generic services and evaluating when a need exists that can only be met through RCEB authorized funding.

* Advocate on behalf of consumers to protect their rights under the law and ensure that they receive those services and benefits to which they are entitled.

* Assist the consumer and family in obtaining essential diagnosis and evaluation from appropriate practitioners and secure written reports and other information which assesses and interprets the consumer's situation.

* Monitor the consumer's health and safety.

* Maintain all documentation and contacts as required by law, regulation and policy.

* Implement RCEB policies and procedures.

* Complete, in a timely manner, functional and/or developmental reviews.

* Keep supervisor informed of the status of the case load and unmet needs in the community.

* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualification:**

**Case Manager I**

* BA Degree in Social Work, Psychology or a related human services field and 2 years similar experience. OR B.A. in an unrelated human services field plus 4 years of experience working directly with the developmentally disabled.

* Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, verbally and in writing.

* Automobile and valid driver's license required.

* Demonstrate cultural awareness and sensitivity and an ability to work effectively with culturally diverse populations.

* Ability to speak in Tagalog.

**Case Manager II**

* Master's Degree in Social Work, Psychology or related human services field.

* Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, verbally and in writing.

* Automobile and valid driver's license required.

* Demonstrate cultural awareness and sensitivity and an ability to work effectively with culturally diverse populations.

* Ability to speak in Tagalog.

**Benefits:**

At the Regional Center of the Easy Bay, we offer a full spectrum of competitive benefits including:

* 3 weeks paid vacation + 12 sick days
* 14 paid holidays + 3 floating holidays
* Multiple options for medical care (including Kaiser at 100% employer paid for employee)
* Dental and vision plans
* CalPERs Retirement (pension),
* Student Loan Forgiveness\*

* Employee Assistance Program, including mental health care

jobs.title: Kids Club Program Leader - Central
jobs.description:
As a Program Leader, you have an opportunity to be a role model for children and to help to create a safe, fun environment for children to grow. You will work as a team member, supervising and interacting with children in a drop-in setting, as well as creating an environment that is safe and activity enriching. The Program Leader will also perform other duties and responsibilities assigned at will as seen fit by the Director.

**SALARY RANGE:** $20.00 - $25.00/hour

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Works with their supervisor to develop and implement age appropriate developmental curriculum.
* Implement age-appropriate enrichment activities according to the weekly plan.
* Model appropriate and constructive discipline.
* Maintain a predetermined personal work schedule covering direct shift hours while the program is open.
* Maintain a clean, fun and engaging environment inside the program while on duty.
* Enforce safety and risk management standards outlined in YMCA training.
* Keep an empowered sense of ownership to maintain quality and good condition of items and equipment in the program.
* Exercise a flexibly responsible mentality when working within the program as not all situations will fit training scenarios.

* Ability to lift and carry objects up to 35 pounds.

**YMCA COMPETENCIES (Leader):**

*Change Leadership:* Facilitates, co-creates, and implements equitable change for the good of the organization and/or community.

*Philanthropy:* Secures resources and support to advance the Y's work.

Description:

The Assistant Case Manager supports the Case Manager in providing compassionate, person-centered services to individuals experiencing homelessness who reside in St. Vincent de Paul of Alameda County’s emergency shelter. Working under the direction of the Case Manager, this position assists guests in identifying and accessing community resources and services that support housing stability and overall well-being. The Assistant Case Manager will work with individuals who may be experiencing complex barriers, including mental health challenges, substance use disorders, domestic violence, unemployment, lack of identification or documentation, and other challenges that may affect their ability to obtain and maintain stable housing.

jobs.description:
Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world's first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads.

Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter!

If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders.

Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light!

Lightmatter's Supply Chain Operations team designs and executes the complex, global manufacturing networks required to build our world-first photonic engines at scale. We partner seamlessly with critical component vendors and Tier-1 manufacturing partners to deliver a resilient, cost-effective, and rapid flow of cutting-edge hardware.

As an Operations Program Manager, you will serve as the primary operational program owner driving supplier execution, Statement of Work governance, and master build planning across silicon foundries, Tier-1/Tier-2 OSATs, and Contract Manufacturers. Operating with high autonomy, you will bridge internal R&D, Packaging Engineering, Quality, and Commercial teams with external vendor leadership to drive NPI builds through to High-Volume Manufacturing.

* Drive end-to-end operational execution for assigned electro-optical program lines by aligning customer and internal demand into master build plans spanning silicon foundries, OSATs, and Contract Manufacturers.
* Build and maintain virtual line-item Clear-To-Build (CTB) matrices across multi-tier suppliers. You will track component lead times and drive consigned material staging into OSAT and CM facilities to guarantee unblocked build execution.
* Partner with engineering leads to draft, enforce, and track vendor Statements of Work. You will conduct weekly operational progress reviews, hold suppliers accountable to milestone deliverables, and drive overall vendor execution metrics.
* Actively track and resolve critical-path dependencies that impact external manufacturing, driving internal teams to provide the design freeze sign-offs, ECO cut-ins, and test scripts required by vendor partners to proceed with production.
* Maintain transparent milestone risk logs, material readiness trackers, and build progress dashboards to consistently communicate program status and critical path risks to executive leadership with actionable mitigation plans.
* Own PLM workflows across the product lifecycle, which includes creating and managing Bills of Materials and directly managing the routing and approval of Engineering Change Orders.

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business Management, Engineering, or a related field, complemented by relevant operational experience.
* 8+ years of progressive experience in Operations Program Management or Partner Operations within high-tech hardware, semiconductors, optical networking, or silicon photonics.
* Proven track record directly managing external manufacturing partners, contract manufacturers, silicon foundries, or OSATs through complex NPI-to-HVM build cycles.
* Advanced expertise constructing multi-tier master schedules, tracking material availability, and enforcing line-item CTB matrices across multi-stage assembly flows.
* Executive presence, influence, and assertiveness necessary to drive both internal engineering teams and external partner program managers to strict milestone dates.
* Hands-on experience executing BOM management, ECO routing, and revision control within PLM systems, alongside working within ERP/MRP environments.

#### **Preferred Qualifications**

* A Master's degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, or a technical discipline is strongly preferred.

**Job Summary**:

The Finance Operations Manager is responsible for the day-to-day management and execution of assigned Finance Operations functions across HNIB. Operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with significant M&A activity, this role takes ownership of core FinOps workstreams, complex operational issues, agency integrations, and process improvements that support the organization’s continued growth.

The position requires hands-on management, strong problem-solving skills, general ledger knowledge, and excellent communication. The Manager is accountable for accurate and timely execution of assigned processes, independently resolving issues, and working closely with Operations and Agency Principals to integrate and streamline newly acquired agencies while maintaining financial integrity.

**Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:**

* Leadership and Team Development

o Manage assigned day-to-day Finance Operations activities across Direct Bill, Cash Receipts, Payables, and related banking functions, with accountability for timely and accurate execution

o Coach and develop FinOps leads and team members, keeping the team engaged and motivated while adjusting responsibilities to foster growth, accountability, and operational knowledge.

o Take ownership of complex operational issues within assigned areas, drive investigations through resolution, and escalate significant risks or decisions as appropriate

o Foster a collaborative environment with clear accountability and follow-through, balancing consistent procedures with the evolving needs of the business.

* Operations, Process & Systems

o Oversee and improve operational workflows, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and audit compliance while adapting to shifting priorities and building scalable processes as the organization grows.

o Coordinate directly with Accounting, IT, Operations, and Finance leadership to execute system and process changes impacting assigned Finance Operations activities

o Maintain clear, current process documentation for assigned Finance Operations functions and ensure procedures are followed as processes evolve

o Drive standardization and efficiency across acquired agencies and operational teams, identifying gaps and implementing practical solutions

o Serve as the primary Finance Operations liaison to Operations for assigned M&A integrations; own the transition of newly acquired agencies into standardized workflows, resolve integration issues, and coordinate with Accounting and agency teams through implementation

o Own year-end procedures and audit deliverables for Finance Operations, ensuring timely completion and resolution of outstanding issues.

* General Ledger & Cash Management

o Apply strong general ledger knowledge to ensure assigned Finance Operations activity is accurately reflected in financial reporting

o Own the investigation and resolution of discrepancies between operational subledgers and the general ledger, coordinating with Accounting counterparts as needed

o Resolve accounting and reconciliation issues arising from operational transactions and guide team members on their financial impact

o Monitor daily cash positions across HNIB and its subsidiaries, identify funding or liquidity needs, and promptly communicate and act on exceptions.

o Coordinate approved movement and sweeping of excess subsidiary cash, ensuring transactions are accurate, timely, and properly recorded

o Proactively identify, investigate, and communicate operational issues affecting cash timing, reconciliations, or financial reporting; drive corrective action

* Team Player and Role Model:

o Be a role model for the finance team, embodying the organization's values and promoting a culture of excellence, integrity, and accountability.

o Communicate clearly, directly, and proactively with agency leaders, Operations, Accounting, and other cross-functional teams; own follow-through on issues and commitments.

Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in Finance, Accounting, or a related business discipline.

**Experience**  
5–7 years of experience in finance, accounting, or financial operations, including 1–3 years of supervisory or management experience. Strong general ledger knowledge, problem-solving skills, and written and verbal communication skills. Experience with M&A integrations, multi-entity operations, or the insurance industry is a plus.

jobs.description:
**Patient Experience & Operations Manager**

**Danville Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics | Danville, CA**  
**Full-time, in person | $70,000–$95,000 annually, depending on experience**  
**Schedule: Monday through Thursday, plus every other Friday**

**Help us make every family feel known, welcomed, and cared for.**

**At Danville Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics, we believe an exceptional dental visit starts before a child ever sits in the dental chair. It starts with a familiar greeting, a thoughtful handoff, and a team that notices the little things.**

**Our established pediatric dental practice has grown, and we’re looking for an outstanding leader to help us preserve the personal attention and warmth that families love while keeping our busy days running smoothly.**

**You might come from dentistry, hospitality, healthcare, or another service-focused business. What matters most is your ability to lead people, anticipate needs, and turn high standards into consistent daily habits.**

**The role: You will be an active, visible presence throughout the pediatric practice, supporting our front desk and clinical teams from arrival through checkout. Working alongside our office manager and doctors, you will oversee daily service, team coordination, and patient flow, while our office manager continues to oversee financial operations.**

**This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll move throughout the office, observe the patient experience, and help the team make thoughtful adjustments throughout the day. You’ll notice when a family needs an update, when a teammate needs support, and when a process needs improvement. You’ll address concerns respectfully and follow through until they are resolved.**

**You’ll also help our practice grow by ensuring we consistently put our best foot forward, create experiences families want to share, and help new patients discover our care through online reviews and word of mouth.**

**What you’ll do**

* Make every welcome personal. Help the team recognize returning families, greet children by name, and make new patients feel comfortable.
* Keep the day moving smoothly. Monitor patient flow, identify delays, coordinate handoffs, and ensure families receive timely updates.
* Coach in the moment. Offer clear, respectful guidance, recognize excellent work, and help team members understand how their actions shape the patient experience.
* Build trust and accountability. Listen to team members, clarify expectations, address recurring concerns privately, and follow up consistently.
* Support the entire visit. Observe how families are welcomed, brought into treatment, and guided through checkout so each step feels thoughtful and organized.
* Lead daily team coordination. Facilitate brief huddles, anticipate challenges, and help teams communicate across departments.
* Handle concerns with care. Listen to families, resolve service issues within your authority, and involve the appropriate doctor or manager when needed.
* Use technology to improve the day. Learn our dental practice software and use available tools to improve efficiency, track follow-through, identify gaps, and strengthen the patient experience.
* Help new families discover our practice. Support practice growth by ensuring we consistently put our best foot forward, from first impressions to follow-up. Coach the team to invite honest online reviews, make it easy for families to share their experiences, and encourage word-of-mouth referrals through thoughtful, memorable care.
* Create lasting improvements. Develop practical service standards, support onboarding, and track patient feedback, timeliness, and progress so improvements become consistent habits.

**Who you are:**

**You are warm, observant, organized, and comfortable taking initiative. You can make a child feel at ease, help a parent feel heard, and have a direct conversation with a team member while preserving their dignity.**

**You know that kindness and accountability belong together. You earn trust by listening, showing up consistently, and following through. You give specific feedback, explain expectations clearly, and check back to make sure improvements last.**

**We’re looking for:**

* Demonstrated experience leading and coaching a team in a busy, service-focused environment.
* A record of improving customer or patient experiences.
* Strong communication, judgment, organization, and follow-through.
* Confidence managing competing priorities and addressing problems calmly.
* Comfort using technology to improve efficiency, track progress, and support excellent service.
* The willingness and ability to learn our dental practice software and use it confidently in daily work after training.
* An appreciation for children and the families who care for them.
* Comfort working in person and moving throughout the practice for much of the day.

**Dental experience is welcome but not required. We encourage applicants with leadership backgrounds in hospitality, guest services, healthcare, retail, and other businesses known for exceptional service. We will provide training in our dental software and office workflows.**

**Why join us?**

**You’ll work alongside an experienced team caring for children and families in the Danville community. This role offers the opportunity to shape the daily experience of our patients, support our team’s growth, and see the impact of your leadership every day.**

**Compensation, schedule & benefits**

* Pay: $70,000–$95,000 annually, depending on experience.
* Schedule: Full-time, Monday through Thursday, plus every other Friday.
* Location: In person at our Danville, CA practice.
* Paid time off (PTO).
* Medical benefits.
* 401(k) opportunities.
* Dental benefits for employees’ children under age 18.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Operations Readiness
jobs.description:
Gatik, the leader in autonomous middle-mile logistics, is revolutionizing the B2B supply chain with its autonomous transportation-as-a-service (ATaaS) solution and prioritizing safe, consistent deliveries while streamlining freight movement by reducing congestion. The company focuses on short-haul, B2B logistics for Fortune 500 retailers and in 2021 launched the world's first fully driverless commercial transportation service with Walmart. Gatik's Class 3-7 autonomous trucks are commercially deployed across major markets, including Texas, Arkansas, and Ontario, Canada, driving innovation in freight transportation.

The company's proprietary Level 4 autonomous technology, Gatik Carrier™, is custom-built to transport freight safely and efficiently between pick-up and drop-off locations on the middle mile. With robust capabilities in both highway and urban environments, Gatik Carrier™ serves as an all-encompassing solution that integrates advanced software and hardware powering the fleet, facilitating effortless integration into customers' logistics operations.

**About the Role**

Gatik is looking for a detail-oriented, highly organized **Program Manager, Operations Readiness** to make sure our operations teams are prepared for every change that reaches the field. In this role, you will manage readiness for software releases, hardware improvements, platform updates, operational process changes, and end-state improvement rollouts, using lean principles and standardized processes. Reporting to the Director of Central Operations, you will act as the primary conduit between Technical Engineering and Operations, and partner closely with Product, Training, and Safety so that every change is enabled, communicated, trained, and validated before launch. You will be instrumental in maintaining safety and operational continuity while driving fast, reliable delivery of improvements across our autonomous fleet.

This role is **hybrid**, **2** days per week in **Santa Clara, Phoenix, Dallas, or Toronto**.

**What You'll Do**

* **Own readiness programs end to end.** Plan and run readiness for software releases, hardware improvements, platform updates, process changes, and end-state rollouts, from early scoping through launch and post-launch stabilization.
* **Standardize the readiness process.** Build and maintain standard work, templates, checklists, and go/no-go gates so every launch follows a consistent, repeatable process.
* **Apply lean principles.** Use lean tools (value stream mapping, waste elimination, root cause analysis) to make readiness and rollout workflows faster, simpler, and less error-prone.
* **Bridge Engineering and Operations.** Act as the conduit between Technical Engineering and Operations: translate technical changes into operational impact, and bring field realities back into engineering priorities.
* **Maintain the operations triage process.** Own the triage process for issues coming out of operations, including intake, prioritization, routing to the right engineering or functional owners, and tracking to resolution.
* **Escalate field feedback.** Collect and synthesize feedback from operations teams, escalate critical issues quickly and clearly, and make sure feedback shapes future releases and improvements.
* **Partner across functions.** Work with Product, Operations, Training, and Safety to align on scope, dependencies, timelines, and owners for each change.
* **Drive training and enablement.** Coordinate with Training to make sure documentation, SOP updates, training content, and field communications are delivered and completed before launch.
* **Manage risk and safety alignment.** Work with Safety to identify operational risks, confirm mitigations are in place, and make sure changes meet safety and regulatory requirements.
* **Coordinate rollouts and close the loop.** Plan phased or market-by-market rollouts, serve as the single point of coordination at launch, and run retrospectives to improve the process.

**What We're Looking For**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 5+ years of experience in program management, operations, or launch management.
* Experience managing cross-functional programs with several stakeholders, including technical engineering teams.
* Experience building or running an issue triage, intake, or escalation process.
* Working knowledge of lean principles and process standardization.
* Experience preparing operations teams for product, technology, or process changes.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, including turning technical information into clear operational guidance.
* Experience with program management and issue tracking tools such as Jira, Confluence, Asana, or Smartsheet.
* Experience in autonomous vehicles, trucking, logistics, or fleet operations preferred.
* Lean Six Sigma Yellow or Green Belt, or equivalent lean training preferred.
* Experience supporting software or hardware release cycles in a technology or robotics environment preferred.
* Familiarity with safety-critical operations and change management processes preferred.
* Experience working with training and enablement teams to roll out SOPs and field training preferred.
* PMP, CSM, or similar program management certification preferred.
* Experience in a high-growth or startup environment preferred.

**More about Gatik**

Founded in 2017 by experts in autonomous vehicle technology, Gatik has rapidly expanded its presence to Mountain View, Dallas-Fort Worth, Arkansas, and Toronto. As the *first and only* company to achieve fully driverless middle-mile commercial deliveries, Gatik holds a unique and defensible position in the AV industry, with a clear trajectory toward sustainable growth and profitability.

We have delivered complete, proprietary AV technology - an integration of software and hardware - to enable earlier successes for our clients in constrained Level 4 autonomy.

**Company Overview**
--------------------

IDMe is the next-generation digital identity wallet that simplifies how individuals securely prove their identity online. Consumers can verify their identity with IDMe once and seamlessly login across websites without having to create a new login and verify their identity again. Over 175 million users experience streamlined login and identity verification with IDMe at 22 federal agencies, 50 state government agencies, and more than 100 healthcare organizations. Over 600 consumer brands use IDMe to verify communities and user segments to honor service and build more authentic relationships. IDMe's technology meets the federal standards for consumer authentication set by the Commerce Department and is approved as a NIST 800-63-3 IAL2 / AAL2 credential service provider by the Kantara Initiative. IDMe is committed to "No Identity Left Behind" to enable all people to have a secure digital identity. To learn more, visit https://network.id.me/.

IDMe is a full-time, in-office culture. Unless a specific job description explicitly states otherwise, all roles are on-site five days per week at one of our offices in McLean, VA; Mountain View, CA; New York City, NY; or Tampa, FL. Certain roles — such as field-based sales or other remote-by-design positions — may have different work arrangements as noted in their individual postings.

At IDMe, we embrace the thoughtful use of AI tools in our daily work and there are even occasions where we leverage AI in our hiring process. However, during the interview process, we want to understand your individual skills and experiences. Therefore, we have guidelines on how AI can be appropriately used during your application and interviews which can be found here.

**About the Role**

ID.me is hiring a Manager of Sales Operations & Deal Desk to be the operational engine behind our sales process — from pipeline hygiene and CRM administration to deal structuring and approvals. This role sits within Revenue Operations and is the day-to-day partner Sales reps and managers turn to for anything that touches process, systems, or deal terms. Given ID.me's consumption-based pricing model, deals often involve non-standard structures — usage tiers, ramp schedules, minimum commitments — that require careful review and consistent governance. This role is a strong fit for someone who's detail-oriented, systems-fluent, and energized by being the person who keeps sales moving efficiently without sacrificing deal quality or compliance.  
Level (Senior Analyst vs. Manager) will be determined based on the candidate's experience.

**Why This Role Matters**

Sales Operations & Deal Desk is where strategy meets execution — every deal that closes efficiently and every clean pipeline report starts here. This role gives you direct, visible impact on how quickly and effectively ID.me's sales team can operate.

**What You'll Do**

Deal Desk

* Review and approve deal structures, pricing exceptions, discounting, and non-standard contract terms in line with company policy
* Partner with Sales, Legal, and Finance to structure deals for ID.me's consumption-based pricing model — usage tiers, minimum commitments, ramp schedules, and renewal terms
* Maintain deal desk approval workflows and playbooks, ensuring consistent turnaround times and clear escalation paths
* Track and report on deal desk cycle time, exception volume, and win/loss patterns tied to deal structure

Sales Operations

* Own CRM data integrity and administration (Salesforce): pipeline hygiene, opportunity stages, fields, and reporting structure
* Support territory design, account assignment, and quota allocation in partnership with Sales leadership
* Build and maintain sales dashboards and reporting for pipeline coverage, forecast accuracy, and rep productivity
* Identify and implement process improvements across the quote-to-cash lifecycle, reducing friction for reps and improving data quality for Finance

Cross-Functional Partnership

* Act as the go-to resource for sales reps and managers on process, systems, and deal questions
* Partner with Finance/FP&A to ensure deal terms and CRM data flow cleanly into revenue reporting and forecasting
* Support onboarding and training for new sales hires on CRM usage, deal desk process, and sales tools
* Assist with ad hoc analysis and projects as Revenue Operations scales

**What You'll Bring**

* 3+ years (Senior Analyst) or 5+ years (Manager) of experience in sales operations, deal desk, or a related analytical function, ideally in B2B SaaS
* Strong hands-on experience with Salesforce (or comparable CRM) — administration, reporting, and workflow configuration
* Strong Excel/spreadsheet skills; comfort building clean, reliable analysis under time pressure
* High attention to detail and a process-oriented mindset — comfortable being the person who enforces consistency
* Clear communicator who can explain policy and process to sales reps without being a bottleneck
* Comfort operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where process is still being built

**Nice to Have**

* Experience with deal structuring for consumption/usage-based pricing models - Experience with CPQ tools or quote-to-cash process design
* Exposure to sales compensation, territory planning, or forecasting

At Coram AI, we’re reimagining video security for the modern world. Our cloud-native platform uses computer vision and AI to help businesses stay safe, make smarter decisions, and move faster; from real-time alerts to seamless clip sharing and multi-site visibility.

You’ll be joining an ambitious, fast-moving team that values clarity, craftsmanship, and impact. Every person here has a voice, ships meaningful work, and helps shape how AI can make the world safer and more connected.

**About the role**
------------------

As a Revenue Operations Manager, you’ll report directly to the Senior Director of Strategy & Operations and own the processes and systems that run Coram’s go-to-market engine. You’ll identify opportunities to improve sales productivity, efficiency, and data accuracy, then design processes and build systems and AI workflows to deliver those improvements. You’ll own this work from initial problem definition through implementation, adoption, and measurable results.

This role combines process design with hands-on systems building. You’ll partner with senior stakeholders across sales, channel, enablement, marketing, and finance to simplify critical GTM processes, administer HubSpot and the sales engagement and dialing stack, and prioritize AI-native automation so the sales team can spend more time selling.

**Responsibilities**

* Build and deploy AI agents, workflows, and automations that eliminate manual work for reps.
* Own CRM data quality and integrations across CRM, sales engagement, dialing, enrichment, conversation intelligence, and finance systems to ensure reliable pipeline, attribution, and partner data.
* Lead implementation and change management for the processes and tools you introduce, ensuring adoption and ongoing maintenance and measuring their impact on rep productivity and data accuracy.

**Skills and qualifications**

* Demonstrated ability to take a process or system problem from an ambiguous starting point through design, implementation, adoption, and measurable improvements in team productivity, efficiency, and accuracy.

* Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills, with the ability to connect tools through APIs, webhooks, or automation platforms.
* Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain tradeoffs plainly to reps, managers, executives, and partners and enforce process requirements when needed.
* Strong ownership and judgment, with the ability to prioritize independently and balance long-term system improvements with immediate business needs.
* Adaptability and resilience in a fast-paced environment with evolving priorities.

* Ability to work on-site five days a week in Sunnyvale, CA.

jobs.title: Program Manager II, Clinical Research Operations, Platforms and Devices
jobs.description:
### **Minimum qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
* 2 years of experience in program or project management.
* Experience integrating generative AI tools or Large Language Model (LLM) interfaces into workflows.
* Experience as a clinical research associate in sponsor-initiated clinical research operations.

  

### **Preferred qualifications:**

* 2 years of experience managing cross-functional or cross-team projects.
* Experience in user experience research and ophthalmic optics, including a strong understanding of ophthalmic terminology, lens measurements, prescription interpretation, and optical measurements and equipment.
* Experience in consumer electronics, or wearables technologies.
* Familiarity with hardware development cycles and processes.

**About the job**
-----------------

A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Program Manager at Google, you’ll lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish — working with stakeholders to plan requirements, manage project schedules, identify risks, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. Your projects will often span offices, time zones, and hemispheres. It's your job to coordinate the players and keep them up to date on progress and deadlines.

As a Clinical Program Manager at Google, you will work with stakeholders to deliver on clinical outcomes and manage device use in alignment with clinical compliance requirements. You will plan study requirements with internal engineering teams and usher user evaluations through the entire product lifecycle. This includes managing Institutional Review Board (IRB) compliance, coordinating laboratory workflows, and communicating with project stakeholders.

You will be responsible for driving the day-to-day operations and logistics of clinical studies, serving as the primary liaison between study sites, managers, and regulatory bodies. Key duties include managing IRB submissions, maintaining the Trial Master File (TMF) to ensure GCP compliance, and coordinating the distribution of investigational devices and study supplies. Additionally, this role oversees subject enrollment tracking, monitors Case Report Form (CRF) data quality, and ensure all participant data, informed consent forms (ICFs), and Adverse Event (AE) reporting are accurate, legible, and fully compliant with ALCOA+ source documentation principles inside the Trial Master File (TMF).

The Platforms and Devices team encompasses Google's various computing software platforms across environments (desktop, mobile, applications), as well as our first party devices and services that combine the best of Google AI, software, and hardware. Teams across this area research, design, and develop new technologies to make our user's interaction with computing faster and more seamless, building innovative experiences for our users around the world.

jobs.description:
Meta is hiring a Reality Labs Product Data Operations Program Manager to run multilingual data collection (DC) for our language expansion work. Reality Labs builds the next generation of computing across Meta's mixed reality, virtual reality, and wearables products. As we bring AI experiences to more languages and regions, the quality, coverage, and speed of our multilingual data shape how well our models understand and respond to people around the world.In this role, you'll take model and product requirements from intake through delivery. For each request, you'll pick the collection model that fits best: in-house collection, scaled vendor collection, or a mix of both. You'll also build DC practices that can scale and repeat across languages and locales. You'll work across functions with research, engineering, product, quality, legal/privacy, and vendor partners. You'll define and enforce quality standards for data deliverables in a fast-moving environment where priorities shift frequently.  
  
  

### **Program Manager, Product Data Operations (Reality Labs) Responsibilities:**

* Own the full lifecycle of language expansion data collection programs, from requirements intake and scoping through collection, quality assurance, and dataset delivery
* Turn model, evaluation, and product requirements into clear collection specs: language and locale coverage, speaker and participant criteria, volume targets, timelines, and acceptance criteria
* Choose the right DC model for each need (in-house, scaled vendor, or hybrid) based on quality, speed, cost, coverage, and risk, and explain the tradeoffs to stakeholders
* Build repeatable DC playbooks, SOPs, templates, and intake standards so that new languages and locales can launch quickly and consistently
* Work closely with research scientists, engineers, TPMs, product, linguists, quality, and privacy partners to align on priorities, dependencies, and success measures
* Develop systems that operationalize data to track throughput, cost, and quality trends. Build dashboards and leadership-facing reporting that drive decisions
* Prioritize competing requests based on impact, urgency, and stakeholder needs. Iterate on plans as model training schedules change, escalate risks early, and ensure that budget targets are met

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining a Bachelor's degree in a directly related field, or equivalent practical experience. Degree must be completed prior to joining Meta
* Bachelor's degree in a directly related field, or equivalent practical experience. Degree must be completed before joining Meta
* 4+ years of experience in program management, data operations or technical operations in a data-driven, AI/ML or technology organization
* Experience in running data collection, annotation, or language data programs, including managing external vendors at scale
* Experience in communicating with and influencing multiple cross-functional stakeholders and leaders
* Experience defining and maintaining quality standards and acceptance criteria for data deliverables
* Analytical experience using data to spot trends, diagnose operational issues, and influence program direction
* Experience prioritizing competing workstreams based on impact and deadlines in fast-moving, agile environments with changing priorities
* Experience breaking ambiguous problems into component parts to develop solutions
* In-person presence at least 3 days per week, with occasional travel required

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience in owning program budgets, cost forecasting, or per-unit cost tracking
* Experience with AI/ML development lifecycles, including model evaluation, benchmarking, and data-centric improvement of model output
* Proficiency in one or more languages besides English, as the role supports multilingual data collection programs across multiple regions and locales
* Track record of building scalable, repeatable operating models or playbooks for a service function
* Experience designing hybrid in-house and vendor sourcing strategies, including cost/quality trade-off analysis
* Experience with participant recruitment, screening criteria, informed consent, and data governance for human-subject data across regions
* Experience with multilingual, speech, text, or conversational AI data, including localization or language expansion programs
* Experience building or deploying automation or AI solutions in production workflows
* Experience in AR/VR, wearables, consumer electronics or AI products

  
  
  

### **About Meta:**

Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. Apps like Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp further empowered billions around the world. Now, Meta is moving beyond 2D screens toward immersive experiences like augmented and virtual reality to help build the next evolution in social technology. WestRock Engineering is a San Francisco based general engineering firm specializing in underground utility infrastructure for public works and Capital Improvement Program (CIP) projects throughout the Bay Area. jobs.description:
About Second Harvest of Silicon Valley  
Founded in 1974, Second Harvest of Silicon Valley is one of the largest food banks in the nation and a trusted nonprofit leader in ending local hunger. The organization distributes nutritious groceries through a network of nearly 400 partners at drive-thru and walk-up sites across Santa Clara and San Mateo counties. Due to the prohibitively expensive cost of living in Silicon Valley, the economic downturn caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, and the rise in inflation, Second Harvest is now serving an average of about 500,000 people every month. Second Harvest also connects people to federal nutrition programs and other food resources, and advocates for anti-hunger policies on the local, state and national levels. To learn more about how Second Harvest is responding to the incredible amount of need in Silicon Valley, visit shfb.org.

About the Position  
The main responsibilities of this role include developing expertise within a particular geographical region, forming deep community relationships, and managing food distribution programs to provide ongoing nutritious food access for low-income individuals and families. Regional Program Managers are experts in their region and act as a primary liaison for a portfolio of 501(c)(3) nonprofit partners and Second Harvest programs. The role manages relationships, ensures collaboration with partners, develops alignment between organizations, and optimizes the food distribution process while leveraging all resources effectively. For Second Harvest programs, the incumbent manages all aspects of food distributions, including onsite operations, volunteer management, and best-in-class client experience. The position dedicates 30-50% of the time to working actively in the community, addressing root causes of hunger, and enhancing community engagement.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Product Data Operations (Reality Labs)
jobs.description:
Meta is hiring a Reality Labs Product Data Operations Program Manager to run multilingual data collection (DC) for our language expansion work. Reality Labs builds the next generation of computing across Meta's mixed reality, virtual reality, and wearables products. As we bring AI experiences to more languages and regions, the quality, coverage, and speed of our multilingual data shape how well our models understand and respond to people around the world.In this role, you'll take model and product requirements from intake through delivery. For each request, you'll pick the collection model that fits best: in-house collection, scaled vendor collection, or a mix of both. You'll also build DC practices that can scale and repeat across languages and locales. You'll work across functions with research, engineering, product, quality, legal/privacy, and vendor partners. You'll define and enforce quality standards for data deliverables in a fast-moving environment where priorities shift frequently.  
  
  

### **Program Manager, Product Data Operations (Reality Labs) Responsibilities:**

* Own the full lifecycle of language expansion data collection programs, from requirements intake and scoping through collection, quality assurance, and dataset delivery
* Turn model, evaluation, and product requirements into clear collection specs: language and locale coverage, speaker and participant criteria, volume targets, timelines, and acceptance criteria
* Choose the right DC model for each need (in-house, scaled vendor, or hybrid) based on quality, speed, cost, coverage, and risk, and explain the tradeoffs to stakeholders
* Build repeatable DC playbooks, SOPs, templates, and intake standards so that new languages and locales can launch quickly and consistently
* Work closely with research scientists, engineers, TPMs, product, linguists, quality, and privacy partners to align on priorities, dependencies, and success measures
* Develop systems that operationalize data to track throughput, cost, and quality trends. Build dashboards and leadership-facing reporting that drive decisions
* Prioritize competing requests based on impact, urgency, and stakeholder needs. Iterate on plans as model training schedules change, escalate risks early, and ensure that budget targets are met

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining a Bachelor's degree in a directly related field, or equivalent practical experience. Degree must be completed prior to joining Meta
* Bachelor's degree in a directly related field, or equivalent practical experience. Degree must be completed before joining Meta
* 4+ years of experience in program management, data operations or technical operations in a data-driven, AI/ML or technology organization
* Experience in running data collection, annotation, or language data programs, including managing external vendors at scale
* Experience in communicating with and influencing multiple cross-functional stakeholders and leaders
* Experience defining and maintaining quality standards and acceptance criteria for data deliverables
* Analytical experience using data to spot trends, diagnose operational issues, and influence program direction
* Experience prioritizing competing workstreams based on impact and deadlines in fast-moving, agile environments with changing priorities
* Experience breaking ambiguous problems into component parts to develop solutions
* In-person presence at least 3 days per week, with occasional travel required

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience in owning program budgets, cost forecasting, or per-unit cost tracking
* Experience with AI/ML development lifecycles, including model evaluation, benchmarking, and data-centric improvement of model output
* Proficiency in one or more languages besides English, as the role supports multilingual data collection programs across multiple regions and locales
* Track record of building scalable, repeatable operating models or playbooks for a service function
* Experience designing hybrid in-house and vendor sourcing strategies, including cost/quality trade-off analysis
* Experience with participant recruitment, screening criteria, informed consent, and data governance for human-subject data across regions
* Experience with multilingual, speech, text, or conversational AI data, including localization or language expansion programs
* Experience building or deploying automation or AI solutions in production workflows
* Experience in AR/VR, wearables, consumer electronics or AI products

  
  
  

### **About Meta:**

Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. ------------

At the County of Marin, our employees overwhelmingly report feeling their work is meaningful, they like the work they do, and they are proud to tell people “I work for the County of Marin.” Discover more about us, our values and our organizational culture on the Department of Human Resources website. Read on to find out more about this opportunity.

**ABOUT THE POSITION**
----------------------

**Flex recruitment:**  
There are currently three (3) full-time, regular hire Capital Planning and Project Manager I/II (CPPM I/II) vacancies in the Capital Projects Division. Candidates will be considered for the level they meet minimum qualifications.

Working under the direction of the Capital Division Manager and in coordination with senior project management staff, the Capital Planning and Project Manager I and II positions support the delivery of Capital Improvement Projects from the planning and design phases through construction and project closeout. These positions provide project coordination and management support to help ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, within approved budgets and schedules, and in accordance with applicable requirements.

The Capital Planning and Project Manager I and II work closely with County project managers, design consultants, contractors, internal departments, and other project stakeholders in the delivery of Capital Projects. jobs.title: Deployment & Engagement Operations Lead
jobs.description:
**Who We Are**
--------------

Physical Intelligence is bringing general-purpose AI into the physical world. We are a group of engineers, scientists, roboticists, and company builders developing foundation models and learning algorithms to power the robots of today and the physically-actuated devices of the future.

**The Team**
------------

This role sits in Research Operations and works closely with partnerships, research, hardware, and infrastructure. Partnerships sets the terms of each engagement and research owns the technical goal. This role owns everything it takes to deliver operationally, from the point an agreement takes shape through completion.

This role requires sound judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and a strong sense of ownership. You will start as a hands-on individual contributor, build the playbook for how PI runs external engagements, and grow the team that supports future partners and deployments.

**About the Role**
------------------

As our work scales, more of it happens alongside external partners and at deployment sites. Each engagement brings its own site, schedule, stakeholders, and constraints. The Deployment & Engagement Operations Lead makes sure these engagements are scoped, staffed, resourced, and delivered successfully, so research and engineering teams can stay focused on the technical work.

**In This Role You Will**
-------------------------

* Own operational scope, resourcing, and execution for external engagements and deployments, from kickoff through completion.
* Translate partner commitments into execution plans that define milestones, owners, staffing, robot allocation, and site requirements.
* Lead complex, long-running engagements involving multiple teams, evolving requirements, and significant operational responsibility.
* Build trusted relationships with partner stakeholders and work through their requirements, approvals, schedules, and site constraints.
* Stand up new sites, bringing together operators, fleet support, equipment, logistics, and site access.
* Plan staffing and coverage across robots, shifts, and locations, and step in directly on site when needed.
* Drive readiness ahead of key milestones, including dry runs, bring-up checks, inventory, and fleet and infrastructure coverage.
* Prioritize and allocate robots, people, and support across concurrent engagements, and flag when a commitment needs to change.
* Keep partners, researchers, and leadership aligned on status, risks, escalations, and decisions.
* Build repeatable playbooks and processes, and grow the team that carries them forward as the work scales.

**What We Hope You'll Bring**
-----------------------------

This role sits at the intersection of program management, field operations, and partner delivery. We're looking for someone who has owned operational outcomes on the ground, can lead several engagements at once, and can step into whichever one needs attention.

* 5+ years of experience in program management, field operations, technical project management, or similar roles.
* Track record of launching and running physical operations, such as opening new sites, markets, or facilities, leading hardware deployments, or running on-site programs for enterprise customers.
* Experience owning delivery of external partners or customer programs end to end.
* Experience staffing and leading teams across shifts and locations.
* Ability to quickly understand technical goals and work through tradeoffs with researchers, engineers, and external partners.
* Strong judgment under pressure, including knowing when to escalate and when to push back on commitments we cannot keep.
* Willingness to travel frequently and work extended stretches on site.

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* Experience supporting AI, robotics, autonomous vehicles, or hardware organizations.
* Experience working within large enterprise partner environments, including confidentiality, approvals, and site access requirements.
* Experience turning one-off launches into a repeatable operating motion.
* Experience building operational processes and scaling teams.
* Familiarity with robotics workflows and teleoperation environments.

Druva is the resilience foundation for the AI enterprise, helping organizations secure and recover from connected risk across data, cyber, identity, and AI.
